title: Notre Dame lands 4-star Roman Igwebuike, lone linebacker commit in No. 2 Class of 2027
content:
SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Notre Dame landed a commitment Saturday from four-star Roman Igwebuike, who became the first linebacker to join the 2027 Irish recruiting class, sitting at No. 2 in the 247Sports Composite rankings.

All it took to get Igwebuike’s commitment was a coaching change, an extra-early evaluation, two decommitments from other prospects, one five-star miss and a lot of patience. Igwebuike, who plays at Mount Carmel High School on the south side of Chicago but lives an hour away in Crown Point, Ind., might feel like an easy catch for Notre Dame, but his recruitment was anything but that.

Notre Dame was among the last of the 46 programs that offered a spot to the 6-foot-3, 220-pound linebacker. A year ago, Igwebuike thought about committing to Tennessee. And then Clemson comfortably led, even after Igwebuike attended Notre Dame’s game against Boise State last October. It wasn’t until his official visit to Notre Dame this summer that the Irish pulled clear of the competition.

“They were one of my last offers, but they had always been talking to me since like one of the first,” Igwebuike said. “It wasn’t really a big deal that they offered me late because they were still one of a few teams who were interested in me early, so I took that as appreciated, but just really wanted to see me in person and get me on campus.”

Notre Dame’s ties to Igwebuike began when Irish linebackers coach Brian Jean-Mary was still on staff at Michigan. The Wolverines weren’t a match for Igwebuike, but he liked what he heard from the veteran assistant, who had been among the first coaches to reach out.

The Irish liked Igwebuike, too, with former linebacker coach Max Bullough giving chase. But Notre Dame had two early 2027 linebacker commitments crowding Igwebuike out. Ellis McGaskin was among the first commitments in the class but flipped to Florida earlier this year. Amarri Irvin took another spot, but he flipped to Virginia Tech this summer. (McGaskin is ranked as the No. 28 linebacker in the 247Sports Composite, while Irvin is slotted at No. 26. Igwebuike is ranked No. 9.)

Even after Notre Dame moved on from McGaskin and Irvin, the Irish chased five-star linebacker Kaden Henderson and were scheduled to get him to campus for an official visit a week after hosting Igwebuike. When Henderson committed to Texas A&M in late June, Notre Dame went hard after Igwebuike, who plays at a high school his mother calls “Notre Dame on steroids.”

“The one thing a lot of people say, and I really notice, is Notre Dame is very similar to Mount Carmel,” Igwebuike said. “Especially with the Catholic part of it and then just the brotherhood of the football team in the community. I really liked the culture there.”

Freshman linebacker Thomas Davis Jr. hosted Igwebuike on his official visit, with freshman defensive end Rodney Dunham pitching in. When Igwebuike transferred to Mount Carmel from Crown Point High School after his freshman season, the family toured the high school during Christmas break and then had to hope they were making the right decision, considering Igwebuike didn’t see the school with students or teammates in the hallways. The only drawback of Mount Carmel was the commute from Northwest Indiana, especially during the offseason when the team stages 5:30 a.m. workouts three days a week.

During Igwebuike’s first months at his new school, that meant getting up before 4 a.m. and having his parents drop him at a teammate’s house in another Indiana town to hitch a ride into Chicago. Igwebuike tried never to miss a workout, even when he got food poisoning the night before one.

“I was just throwing up like every 10 minutes, and we finally made it here,” he said. “I did the workout, and then I went home right after. You could kind of tell it’s a big deal to be here. Everybody takes it seriously.”

That mindset should make Igwebuike an easy fit at Notre Dame, where defensive recruiting has hit new levels under head coach Marcus Freeman. The Irish have commitments from five-star defensive linemen David Folorunsho and Abraham Sesay. Last cycle, the Irish added five-star defensive backs Joey O’Brien and Khary Adams, plus Dunham along the defensive line.

That all should put Igwebuike in position to keep doing what he’s done the past two seasons at Mount Carmel: The Caravan have gone 25-3 under the direction of former Northern Illinois quarterback and 2013 Heisman finalist Jordan Lynch.

“I want to be a part of winning. I can’t lose. I hate losing,” Igwebuike said. “But then also like an actual team, I want a team that sticks together. And one that can really take it all away.”

Igwebuike said the first Notre Dame game he watched with the Irish in mind as a potential landing spot was the win over Indiana in the 2024 College Football Playoff first round. The first Irish game he saw in person was Notre Dame’s season-opening loss at Miami last fall, while Igwebuike was on a gameday visit to see the Hurricanes.

“You were able to tell how the players played together,” Igwebuike said. “Even when times got hard, even though they lost, nobody was pointing fingers. They stuck together.”

Now, after a recruiting journey that never felt like a straight line, Igwebuike will be part of that group.
